title: Autopsy and Alibi
premise: True-crime podcaster Isandro Whitlock has spent three years chasing the 1971 disappearance of heiress Marguerite Vale, the coldest unsolved case in the county's records. When a fresh corpse surfaces wearing clothes lifted from Isandro's own closet, staged to mirror a detail from her unreleased final episode, she realizes someone inside her circle is using the case file as a murder script. As bodies accumulate in patterns only she can decode, Isandro discovers the killer is Marguerite's secret grandchild, raised on stolen inheritance documents and nursing a grievance against everyone who profited from the erasure. In the climax, Isandro baits the killer with a fake episode revealing the true will, forcing a confrontation in the sealed east wing of Vale House where Marguerite actually died; the killer confesses, and Isandro chooses to broadcast the truth about the family's corruption rather than the killer's identity, finally finding where she herself belongs.
about_author: Freya Eriksen is a former forensic archivist who spent a decade cataloguing cold-case evidence before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted boathouse on the Oslofjord, where the fog does half her plotting for her.

chapters.title: The Coldest File
chapters.summary: Isandro, in her POV, records the finale of her podcast series on the 1971 Vale disappearance, laying out the case's tangled heirs and missing evidence. A listener voicemail hints someone knows more than police ever did. The beat is confident momentum shadowed by unease — she feels watched as she locks up the studio.

chapters.title: Dressed in My Clothes
chapters.summary: Police call Isandro to identify clothing found on a Jane Doe: her own missing blazer and scarf. Detective Sergeant Rhea Okonkwo, wary but needing her archive knowledge, lets her see the scene. Isandro recognizes staging details from her unpublished draft. The emotional beat is violation — the case has reached into her private life.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Had a Copy
chapters.summary: Isandro audits who had access to her research: her producer Theo, researcher Camille, archivist Bram, and a handful of superfans. Each interview yields alibis that are slightly too polished. Her POV; the beat is creeping paranoia as she realizes the killer may be someone she trusts daily.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Wore
chapters.summary: Flashback-structured chapter through Isandro's narration of old interviews with the late housekeeper, revealing Marguerite Vale was pregnant when she vanished. The dead woman's staging echoes this hidden detail. The beat is revelation — the case is not what anyone, including Isandro, thought it was.

chapters.title: A Second Body, A Second Costume
chapters.summary: A retired detective who worked the original case is found dead, dressed in items traced to Isandro's storage unit. Okonkwo now suspects Isandro herself. Isandro's POV under interrogation; the beat is fear curdling into isolation as the trap closes around her.

chapters.title: The Superfan Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: Isandro investigates listener 'ValeWatcher,' whose forum posts predicted each staging detail before it happened. She traces the account to a defunct internet café near Vale House. Theo's POV briefly shows him deleting something. The beat is pursuit energy undercut by a first hint of betrayal.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: Digging into probate records, Isandro finds a sealed second will naming an unborn child. The current Vale heirs — cousins Aldous and Petra — stonewall her elegantly. Her POV; the beat is righteous anger at how wealth buried the truth, deepening the theme of corrupted power.

chapters.title: Camille's Silence
chapters.summary: Camille admits she leaked research to an anonymous 'documentary partner' months ago, then begs Isandro not to tell Okonkwo. Isandro agrees, compromising herself. The beat is guilt and complicity — Isandro realizes protecting people may be costing lives.

chapters.title: The East Wing Sealed
chapters.summary: Isandro breaks into shuttered Vale House and finds the east wing preserved since 1971, including a nursery no report ever mentioned. Someone has been living there recently. Her POV; the beat is dread and awe — the past literally kept in a room.

chapters.title: Petra's Bargain
chapters.summary: Petra Vale offers Isandro exclusive access to family papers in exchange for burying the pregnancy angle. Isandro refuses, burning the bridge. Petra's POV reveals she knows the killer's name and is terrified. The beat is moral testing — belonging offered at the price of truth.

chapters.title: Episode Zero
chapters.summary: Isandro discovers a pilot episode file she never released has been downloaded by someone using her own credentials. Theo's POV shows his panic as his secret unravels. The beat is vertigo — the killer isn't just reading the file; they've been inside her machine.

chapters.title: Bram's Archive
chapters.summary: Archivist Bram reveals he sold Marguerite's letters years ago to a private buyer whose courier matched Theo's description. Isandro confronts Theo; he denies everything too smoothly. Her POV; the beat is heartbreak — the person who anchored her now anchors her suspicion.

chapters.title: Aldous Confesses to Nothing
chapters.summary: Aldous Vale, dying of illness, tells Isandro he burned the real will decades ago to protect the family name — but swears Marguerite's child died at birth. His certainty cracks when shown the nursery photos. The beat is the collapse of the official story and rising stakes.

chapters.title: The Third Staging
chapters.summary: Camille is attacked and left alive, dressed in Isandro's coat, a message: stop, or the next one dies. Isandro, wracked with guilt, goes off-book with Okonkwo. The beat is grief weaponized into resolve — she stops investigating and starts hunting.

chapters.title: Born in Winter
chapters.summary: Hospital records and a midwife's deathbed letter confirm the child lived and was quietly adopted out. Isandro cross-references adoption registries with podcast donor lists and gets one impossible match. Her POV; the beat is the thrill of the hunt turning cold as the name appears.

chapters.title: The Name in the Donor List
chapters.summary: The match points to someone embedded in Isandro's own production — the killer has been funding the podcast that could expose them, wanting control of the narrative. Isandro says nothing, setting a counter-trap. The beat is icy composure masking terror.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Murder
chapters.summary: Isandro announces a 'lost tape' episode revealing the true will's contents, recording it alone as bait. Okonkwo stakes out the studio; the killer takes the bait differently than planned, targeting the archive instead. The beat is high tension and partial failure — the plan works too well.

chapters.title: Theo's Alibi Breaks
chapters.summary: Okonkwo arrests Theo on courier evidence, but Isandro spots inconsistencies proving Theo was paid to be visible — a decoy. The real killer engineered his downfall. Her POV defending the man she suspected; the beat is humility and clarity about who truly scripted everything.

chapters.title: The Grandchild of Vale House
chapters.summary: Isandro confronts the killer — Camille, Marguerite's secretly adopted granddaughter, raised on stolen letters and disowned twice over. Camille explains the murders as restitution for an inheritance denied. The beat is terrible empathy; Isandro understands her completely and must still stop her.

chapters.title: East Wing, Last Light
chapters.summary: Lured by Camille to Vale House with proof of the original will, Isandro is nearly made the final 'exhibit.' Using her encyclopedic knowledge of the case file, she turns Camille's own staging logic against her until Okonkwo arrives. The beat is visceral climax — the archive literally saves her life.

chapters.title: What the Microphone Heard
chapters.summary: Camille, arrested, asks Isandro to air the whole truth. Isandro produces the final episode: not the killer's confession, but the family's fifty-year cover-up, letting institutions fall instead of one broken woman. The beat is moral resolution — justice reframed as exposure.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Marguerite is reburied under her own name beside the nursery window; the estate passes to public trust. Isandro, changed, starts a new series about the erased rather than the infamous, with Theo restored and Okonkwo a friend. The beat is quiet peace — she has stopped chasing cases and started keeping promises.
